origin: Originally the board at the front of a carriage that stopped mud from dashing up. Through car instrument panels, it came to mean a screen for seeing many states at a glance.
whenToUse: Screens for regularly checking metrics such as sales or visits.
It should read in the order summary, trend, details.
People change the period to compare.
whenNotToUse: There are only one or two metrics (one card is enough).
You'd line up every chart at the same size (importance is lost).
accessibility: Metric cards are a list, so their count is read along with them, and changes are written as "up" or "down".
Arrows and colors are supporting cues, so they're aria-hidden.
Charts say what they show in a figcaption.
Period buttons announce their state with aria-pressed.
